requests.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: v150 authored whole-body mechanic animation atlas for an existing battlefield game.
Create ONE original transparent PNG sheet containing exactly TWELVE painted animation cels in a regular FOUR-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid. All twelve invisible cells have identical dimensions; read left to right, top to bottom. Aim for 1254x1254 pixels or a higher-resolution SQUARE canvas. At 1254 square each cell is approximately 313.5 pixels WIDE and 418 pixels HIGH. The grid cells are equal rectangles. Do not draw cell outlines.
Subject and style: The SAME adult modern infantryman in every cel, full body seen strictly in SIDE PROFILE facing RIGHT. Match the identity and grounded realistic painted material finish of the previously viewed v148/v149 olive infantry art: muted olive/tan camouflage, olive tactical helmet, vest and pouches, gloved hands, dark boots, natural adult anatomy and joints, detailed fabric folds and restrained metal highlights. Crisp readable silhouettes compatible with pixel-scale game display, but no chunky or programmatically constructed pixel anatomy. A small rifle stays securely SLUNG BACK behind the shoulder, untouched, with consistent size and attachment; never aimed or fired.
Action and props: He is doing subtle mechanical wrench/ratchet work on an INVISIBLE vehicle just to his RIGHT. Draw the actor and his held tool ONLY. ONE compact dark-steel ratchet wrench is gripped by the RIGHT gloved hand throughout. Its short metal handle and small recognizable tool head remain attached to that hand. The left hand braces close to the work point or steadies the tool. The wrench HEAD stays at exactly the SAME stationary work point forward of the body in every cel, as if engaged with an invisible fastener; the handle pivots through a SMALL arc while wrist, elbow and shoulder articulate. Do not draw the fastener, vehicle, track, work surface or environmental support.
Exact chronological movement: twelve distinct subtle intermediates, not repeated still figures. Cels 0-2 establish the grip and begin a small clockwise leverage movement; cels 3-5 progressively pull with modest effort; cels 6-8 reset the wrist/ratchet handle without moving the wrench head; cels 9-11 ease back toward the starting grip and close the loop. Cel 11 is a near-start in-between that flows smoothly back to cel 0. Only local arm, wrist, hand and slight shoulder articulation changes; preserve posture and planted contacts. No broad waving, overhead reach or body-height change.
Registration and space: Fixed camera, anatomical scale, baseline and contact center in ALL twelve cells. Never change framing or enlarge individual cels. Keep the ENTIRE body, both boots, helmet, slung rifle, hands and wrench inside its own cell, with at least SIXTEEN genuinely empty transparent pixels on EVERY side at 1254x1254 output, proportionally more if rendered larger. No touching adjacent figures, no clipped rifle or tool. Use the same local ground-contact baseline at y=360 within each 418-pixel-tall row cell at 1254-square output; scale that registration proportionally for larger output. The baseline is invisible and must not be drawn.
Background: Genuine transparent RGBA alpha, empty space alpha exactly zero, with clean edges. No opaque backdrop, haze, checkerboard, ground, floor, baked shadow, base or platform. No vehicle, scenery, additional people, loose or floating tools, sparks, muzzle flash, bandages, dressings, medical pouches in hand, gun reloads, climbing, signaling, labels, text, frame numbers, grid lines, borders or watermarks. This must clearly read as compact mechanical torque-and-reset work.

POSTURE: STANDING MECHANIC. The soldier stands with a slight, constant forward inclination, both feet firmly planted at exactly the same coordinates for all twelve cels. Same leg shape, knee angles, pelvis height, head height and body anchor throughout. No squat, knee dip, stepping, climbing or kneeling. He works at a stationary point forward of his waist/lower chest, with both arms low and elbows naturally bent. Right hand gently works the ratchet handle; left hand braces nearby. The wrench head remains fixed while the handle makes a modest clockwise pull and reset. Keep the compact slung-back rifle out of the working hands.
At 1254-square output, make the full standing body about 270 pixels high within each 418-pixel-tall cell, leaving ample transparent room above and below; use natural adult proportions. Preserve that exact body scale across all twelve cels. The silhouette and wrench-work gesture should remain legible when the game displays the standing actor at about 64 pixels high. Render exactly twelve STANDING mechanic cels, four columns by three rows, on one transparent sheet.

caveats: All three unchanged originals are 1254x1254 RGBA with genuine alpha 0-255 and twelve whole-body cels in a 4x3 layout.

Standing height is approximately 368-370 pixels rather than the requested approximately 270 pixels. Its significant-alpha silhouette has 16 pixels bottom clearance and stable bottom y402, rather than the requested baseline y360.

Kneeling height is approximately 290-291 pixels rather than approximately 190 pixels. Significant-alpha right-cell clearance is only 9-11 pixels, below the required 16. Bottoms drift slightly from y364 to y366.
Prone silhouettes are approximately 96-105 pixels high and 271-296 pixels wide. Many cells have only 7-10 pixels of significant-alpha horizontal clearance, below the requested 16 pixels.
Prone row registration is not fixed: local silhouette bottoms are about y287 in the first row, y261-269 in the second, and y235 in the third, a maximum difference of about 52 pixels.

The ratchet head visibly changes position in the standing and prone sequences instead of remaining at one fixed work point. The kneeling work point appears more stable, but exact head/hand registration has not been measured.
No vehicle, environment, floor, labels, visible grid or floating detached tool was observed. The tools remain hand-held and the rifles remain slung on the back.
Several returning poses are very similar; exact loop closure and readability at 64/43/20-pixel game display sizes were not playback-tested.
All per-cell bounding-box and margin measurements use alpha >16 and exclude fainter edge pixels; they do not certify fully alpha-zero gutters.
